study_type: post-hoc forensic reassessment, not independent confirmation
question: Is the Task 9 spike gate reference floor consistent with the 0.025 ms voltage sampling approximation?

methods.right: 40 steps of 0.025 ms at V_(n+1), exact Task 9 reproduction
methods.right_refined_5: five constant-V substeps per recorded interval; negative control for substep count
methods.linear_5: five midpoint samples of piecewise-linear voltage in each 0.025 ms interval
methods.linear_20: twenty midpoint samples of piecewise-linear voltage in each interval

analysis: Same 350 already-selected Task 9 paths, same initial and teacher endpoint states, train split only. Report m,h,m²h RMSE and signed/absolute error for every existing site/regime group; no candidate model retraining or selection.
preflight: Reproduce Task 9 global right-endpoint m,h,m²h RMSE within 1e-10; right_refined_5 equals right within 1e-10. Otherwise stop before interpretation.
predeclared_interpolation_gate: All four spike groups: linear_20 m RMSE <=50% of right RMSE, max(m,h RMSE)<=0.005, and max gate difference linear_5-vs-linear_20<=0.001.
interpretation_limit: If the gate passes, results are consistent with sampling loss, not proof of the true unobserved intra-sample voltage path. If it fails, the floor remains unresolved and a small denser authentic teacher capture is required. No LUT or full-model claim from this forensic run.
